depth: Across the five frames, the depth map traces the camera wearer moving from a doorway (~3–5 m ahead in frame 1) past a glass partition (~3–5 m in frame 2) into an office corridor (frame 3) before turning to face a person standing directly in front at ~3–5 m (frames 4–5). segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete background entities across the last three frames while leaving the doorway and motion-blurred glass in frames 1 and 2 completely unlabelled. In frame 3, it detects a nearby person on the near right (~0.5–1.5 m away, partially occluded by the right frame edge) and misclassifies the left-side lounge area (~0.5–1.5 m away) as a 'tv' mask, while missing the architectural walls, partition, and furniture entirely. While segmentation sharply delineates the distant person's silhouette and outstretched right arm from the cluttered foreground sofa (~0.5–1.5 m in front to the right) better than the dark RGB clothing, it is unreliable for scene layout, misses the coffee cup in frame 4, and produces detached false-positive 'person' fragments on the upper-right foreground in frames 4 and 5.
pose: The pose map is completely blank for frames 1 through 4, providing no spatial information about the room layout, objects, the nearby person in frame 3, or the distant standing person in frame 4 despite their torso and hand being clearly visible ~3–5 m away in the RGB image. Only in frame 5 does a skeleton appear on the left side of the frame for the person standing ~3–5 m in front of the camera wearer, showing their torso facing away from the camera wearer and their right arm extending downward and to the right out of arm's reach (~3–5 m) where a magenta hand skeleton grasps the paper bag at the bottom edge. This skeleton makes the exact joint articulation of the person's right arm and fingers on the bag explicit despite dark clothing and motion blur in the RGB image. However, the pose map is highly unreliable across the sequence: it fails to detect any keypoints in the first four frames, and in frame 5 the cropped head and occluded lower body cause the estimator to hallucinate a compressed vertical torso with two upward-pointing neck/head segments and folded lower-limb keypoints bunched at the bottom edge.
